Hi folks, I've been coming across a few model F boards for under 50 bucks, but they all seem very discolored (yellowed or browning) on both the case and caps.

The caps seem cheap enough to just replace from Unicomp and others, but what about the springs and case? Basically I just want to know what I'm getting myself into, hoping someone here has a little experience with these!
Difficulty Level in Restoring IBM Model F Keyboards?

Sounds like a good project!

The keyboard case you can sort out with Retr0bright, it's a solution you rub on the yellowed plastic to return it to its natural white colour. Here's step by step instructions on how to Retr0bright. It's not a hard job, but does require quite a bit of time and concentration as you don't want the retr0bright solution to dry (otherwise you get a swirly patten).

You could retr0bright the caps, but I'd just buy new ones from Unicomp. ;)

As for the springs, you can get replacement ones from Unicomp here. The best method would most likely be 'Sandy's Chopstick' method, which involves litterally pulling the springs out and pushing them back in with chopsticks... sounds clumsy but otherwise you'd have to take the plate apart and be forced to do a bolt mod. Ripster has a fantastic guide on the chopstick method which he's dubbed "ChopstickOdeath".

Overall I wouldn't say it's a super hard task but it requires a lot of concentration and effort. I've never tried the retr0bright my self, but my tip for the chopstics (if you do use that method) is not to use too much force when twisting, pulling or pushing, let the spring come loose in its own time. Best of luck if you do start a project!

Awesome info, the Retr0bright looks straightforward enough, I've done some trim restoration on old cars and the process isn't all that different. Most of the springs seem OK, so I think a little work is worth saving half the price of a pristine one. I'll definitely post some pictures of the progress!

That's super, glad I could help. Restoring the board adds to the fun of owning it, the same with restoring old cars!

If you run into any troubles don't hesitate to stop by and ask, I look forward to pictures too, best of luck!

Just finished mine. Custom "Super-Soarer" PCB and cable. You can buy pre-made cables with internal Soarer converters. I wanted custom indicator LEDs, so I made my own.

https://instagram.com/p/50YABrJpR_/?taken-by=samwisekoi

You can buy keycaps from Unicomp, but they won't match the originals. So the best plan is to buy a full set of Unicomp keycaps ($30) and swap out entire sections so the colors and legends match.

If you can, try and get an F-122 that has working switches. The chopstick method works, but it isn't for early adopters. And a full bolt-mod is a BIG project.

Having said all of that, using an F-122 as a daily driver is awesome! And using the Soarer software, you can assign commonly-used functions or macros to all of those extra keys! It is great.

I'll post pics of mine here, on INstagram, and/or GeekHack Real Soon Now.

Good luck!

p.s. Think of the yellowing (not the dirt, the yellowing) as patina. :^D
